title: People Whose List of Favorite Companies Is Not a Subset of Another List
summary: Given an array where each element is a list of favorite companies for a person, identify and return the indices of people whose list of favorites is not completely included within any other person's list of favorites, in ascending order.
statement: Given an array where each element is a list of favorite companies for a person, identify and return the indices of people whose list of favorites is not completely included within any other person's list of favorites, in ascending order.
constraints: Each person lists distinct company names.
Return ascending indices whose list is not a subset of any other person’s list.
hints: Convert each favorite list to a set.
For each person, test containment in every different person’s set.
Keep the index only when no such superset exists.
Set <= handles both proper and equal subsets, while the distinct-index check avoids self-containment.
editorial: Set <= handles both proper and equal subsets, while the distinct-index check avoids self-containment.

tests.explanation: Indices zero, one, and four are not contained in another list.
The first list is excluded as a subset; indices one and two remain.
